children: Twelve of the 24 S&P 500 Materials-sector companies have reported third-quarter 2026 results this week. On the earnings front, four companies fell short of analyst expectations, while six missed revenue estimates.
Here’s a look at how the companies performed:
Among the major reporters, Freeport-McMoRan
, which carries a 5.6% weighting in the index, topped Wall Street expectations on both earnings and revenue.
Freeport-McMoRan

Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.88, beating consensus by $0.05. Revenue increased 8.3% year-over-year to $7.55 billion, exceeding estimates by $150 million. The performance was supported by higher realized prices of $6.54 per pound for copper and $4,273 per ounce for gold.
LyondellBasell

mixed results, with both earnings and revenue falling short of expectations. Adjusted EPS of $2.54 missed consensus by $0.01, while revenue increased 10% year-over-year to $8.50 billion but came in $390 million below estimates. The chemical producer faced weaker demand and lower polymer prices but generated $1.7 billion in operating cash flow and completed a planned €500 million debt repayment.
Nucor

its strongest quarterly performance in more than three years, supported by robust domestic demand and higher realized steel prices. The steelmaker reported Q3 revenue of $11.25 billion, up 32% year-over-year and $460 million above consensus. However, adjusted EPS of $5.80 missed analyst expectations by $0.03. Steel mill shipments exceeded 7.2 million tons, while free cash flow reached $1.6 billion. Management expects fourth-quarter earnings to remain stable or increase modestly from Q3 levels. Nucor shares gained approximately 5% following the results.
Linde

reported record third-quarter results, with sales rising 9.3% year-over-year to $9.4 billion and adjusted diluted EPS increasing 9% to $4.59. Both figures exceeded Wall Street expectations, with earnings beating by $0.07 and revenue by $240 million. Growth was supported by a 5% increase in underlying sales, including a 15% rise in the electronics end market. Backed by an $11 billion project backlog, Linde raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS growth outlook to 8%-9%.
Sherwin-Williams

delivered mixed Q3 results, with consolidated net sales rising 7.9% year-over-year to $6.86 billion, ahead of analyst estimates. Adjusted diluted EPS of $3.63, however, missed consensus of $3.69, reflecting pressure from higher raw material costs, supply chain expenses and acquisition-related dilution. The company narrowed its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $11.85-$12.15 and expects uneven demand conditions to persist into 2027.
Materials Earnings Calendar: Eight Companies Reporting Next Week
Eight S&P 500 Materials-sector companies are scheduled to report earnings next week, spanning three industries.
The Chemicals industry accounts for the largest share, with five companies on the calendar: Albemarle
, Mosaic
, Air Products and Chemicals
, CF Industries Holdings
and International Flavors & Fragrances
. The Containers & Packaging industry has two scheduled reporters: Amcor
and Ball Corp.
. Meanwhile, Martin Marietta Materials
is the sole company from the Construction Materials industry scheduled to report next week.
